constraints.lineLayout: Exactly two lines: n, then n integers separated by single ASCII spaces. Final line terminator optional; LF or CRLF accepted (official tests are CRLF); bare CR, tabs, repeated/leading/trailing spaces, signs, leading zeros and blank lines rejected.
constraints.output: One integer token; unique answer, token comparison exact.
constraints.answerUpperBound: At most 21 distinct ORs end at each index because a_i < 2^20, so answer ≤ min(21n, 2^20).

oracle.efficient: Maintain the set of ORs of subarrays ending at index i: E_i = {a_i} ∪ {a_i | x : x ∈ E_{i-1}}; |E_i| ≤ 21. Union all E_i. O(21 n) time.
independentReferences: _brute_answer: recompute OR of every interval from scratch with three nested loops (no reuse of prefix ORs or ending sets). Used for n ≤ 300.

_last_bit_answer: per-bit last occurrence positions; extend from index i leftwards by distinct last positions, OR-ing in the bits whose last occurrence is at each position. Used for the eight n = 10^5 cases.
bruteDomains: 600 fixed-seed (2431601) random sequences n ≤ 40 with masks 7/63/1023/10^6.
All 170 authored cases: 162 with n ≤ 300 against _brute_answer, 8 maximum against _last_bit_answer.

generatedSuite.coverage: n=1 with 0/1/2/2^19/999999/10^6; zeros, repeated maximum, non-contiguous-OR traps ([1,2,4], [1,0,4]), all 20 powers ascending/descending, bit-19 values near 10^6, small fixed-seed random 0..15, sparse single-bit sequences, full-range random up to n=300, two-bit values; eight legal n=100000 cases (all 10^6 answer 1, all zero answer 1, cyclic powers answer 381, powers with zeros 602, random full range 146960, random single bits 378040, values just below 10^6 1008, arithmetic progression 131889).
generatedSuite.qualificationStatus: Authored cases only. No 5AC/5-genuine-WA or sixth external oracle execution and no independent signoff.

sourceMotivatedCoverage.observation: Extends the cumulative set of all values seen (s = s.union(ns)) instead of only subarrays ending at the previous index, so it counts ORs of non-contiguous subsets; [1,2,4] gives 7 instead of 6. Unit test reimplements this mistake (not the downloaded code) and confirms ≥20 authored cases distinguish it.
Inner loop ORs from the start of the whole array for every i, producing non-interval ORs; covered by non-contiguous traps and random small cases.
Inserts index i into the set and prints len+1; covered by cases where values differ from indices ([2,1,0,0], [6,3,5,0]).
Loops to n inclusive (index error) and inserts indices; covered by the same index-vs-value cases.
Reads only the first line (n) as the sequence; any case with answer != 1 distinguishes it.
Correct-but-quadratic interval enumeration (or n×n matrices). Maximum-size cases expose TLE/memory only; TLE-only kills are not algorithmic proof and must not be counted as genuine WA.
Accepted last-bit-position method over 20 bits with bool r[1111111]; 10^6 < 2^20 so values with bit 19 (524288..10^6) are in range. Included bit-19 and 10^6 boundary cases.
